texts.preamble: Martin A.Kuzhivelikkalam vs The State Of Kerala on 21 March, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 21St Day Of March 2016/1St Chaithra, 1938 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 1622 of 2009 --------------------------------- Crl.A 405/2006 of Addl.Sessions Court (Adhoc)-Ii, Pathanamthitta Cc 65/2003 of C.J.M.Pathanamthitta Revision Petitioner(S)/Accused: -------------------------------------------------- Martin A.Kuzhivelikkalam, S/O. Antony Kuzhivelikkalam, Kuzhivelikkalam House, Kumbanad P.O. Pathanamthitta District. By Advs.Sri.A.M.Abdul Raheem Sri.N.A.Muraleedharan Respondent/Respondent: ----------------------------------------------- 1. The State Of Kerala, Represented By Its Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala Ernakulam. 2. R.Mehaboob, Food Inspector, Thiruvalla Circle. R1 & R2 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 21-03-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Martin A.Kuzhivelikkalam vs The State Of Kerala on 21 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18359865/ 1 B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. No.1622 of 2009 - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - Dated this the 21st day of March 2016 O R D E R
texts.facts: The accused in C.C.No.65 of 2003 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Pathanamthitta filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1)(a)(i), 2(ia)(i) and 7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 29 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 31.7.2001, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 1= Kg. of banana chips from the shop of the revision petitioner. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P14 report stating that the sample contained synthetic food colour tartarzine and therefore, the same was adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the revision petitioner, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P16 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample contained synthetic food colour tartarzine in contravention of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P21 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined for the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P16 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P16 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Martin A.Kuzhivelikkalam vs The State Of Kerala on 21 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18359865/ 2 Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
